draft.title: Neuroplasticity
card: Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to change its structure and function in response to experience. Connections between neurons can form, strengthen, weaken or be lost.
Learning a new skill, such as a language or an instrument, strengthens the connections used. Connections that are rarely used can weaken.
The brain can also change after injury. Nearby areas may take on some of the work of a damaged area, although recovery varies and is not always complete.
Learning, exercise, sleep and social contact help keep the brain working well. These habits support the brain's ability to change.
draft.remember: The brain keeps changing with experience and injury, and healthy habits support that change.
